trails.why: From Falmenta to Alpe Fornà and Piè Zeda going up the Scalinata. Halfway traverse up to the Rio Falmenta, then steep climb in an alpine environment.

trails.name: Cammino dei Petali

trails.name: Tossicia - Cerchiara

trails.why: An ecopsychology loop on Monte di Brianza, with stations for practices of deep reconnection with nature.

trails.name: Percorso BLU - Pianezze
trails.why: A varied route on paths and lanes through fields, hamlets and woods, with gentle climbs.

trails.name: Sentiero Ferla – Bivio Pianetti
trails.why: From the Pianetti picnic area above Cefalù through a cork-oak and holm-oak wood to the top of Pizzo Sant'Angelo at 1,080 m.

trails.name: Percorso dei Pradéi
trails.why: A loop through the Pradéi valley and the Valle Bruciata, south of Palazzago.

trails.name: Le vie del Misma

trails.name: Alta Via n. 1 della Valle d'Aosta - Tappa 16

trails.name: Tossicia - Cusciano
trails.why: A hike of cultural and natural interest through villages, fields, and trails. Points of cultural interest include Tossicia, the ruins of the Franciscan convent, Azzinano and its murals, and Cusciano.

trails.name: Alta Via n. 2 della Valle d'Aosta - Tappa 11

trails.why: Part of the Alta Via della Valle d'Aosta, the high-level hiking route through the Aosta Valley.

trails.why: From the Prati di Ghina to the Alpe Cavrua and Pogallo as far as Cicogna, this is an easier route than the overcoming of Cima Sasso, but the path search difficulties are superior

trails.name: T741 - Ruinas - Punta La Marmora
trails.why: An interesting route to Punta La Marmora. After an initial stretch on a dirt road, the trail winds through a small valley filled with water and trees.

trails.name: Periplo del Pizzo Arera
trails.why: From Rifugio Capanna 2000 the path leaves the summit route and crosses the Val d'Arera.

trails.name: Giro di Paltrac
trails.why: Discover Giro di Paltrac, an easy ring tour almost exclusively on the road from Val de Fornas to Paltrac.

trails.name: Via Francigena - Variant Sutri
trails.why: The Via Francigena is an ancient road and pilgrimage route running from the cathedral city of Canterbury in England, through France and Switzerland, to Rome and then to Apulia, where there were the ports of embarkation for the Holy Land.

trails.name: M39 - Folsogno - Bocchetta di Sant'Antonio
trails.why: Interesting and pleasant trip up to La Cailina from which it is possible make return with a circular route to Alpe Blizz and then following the M37, beyond it becomes very tiring and difficult to follow and intended for expert hikers

trails.name: GTA: Santuario San Giovanni - Oropa
trails.why: The Grande Traversata delle Alpi is a long-distance hiking trail in the Italian region of Piedmont.

trails.name: S03 'Via delle Genti': tratto Cannobio - Cannero Riviera
trails.why: Historic "Via delle Genti", route from Cannobio to Cannero. Evocative villages and lush woods.

trails.name: Le tese di Pimonte
trails.why: From Quisisana near the Fontane del Re, on slightly exposed stretches towards Monte Coppola, over the old bridge of the Bourbon aqueduct to the Monte Coppola saddle.

trails.name: Alta Vista
trails.why: The route offers wide views over the plain and passes through very different woods, shaped by altitude and exposure.

trails.name: Agritour dea Molonara (percorso giallo)
trails.why: The Agritour dea Molonara is a 24 km route, open to all year-round, through the countryside of Schio, Marano Vicentino and Zanè, rediscovering rural sights close to home.

trails.name: Cammino della Regina Camilla - Tappa 3
trails.why: A short stage from Roccagorga past the church of Sant'Eleuterio to Maenza.

trails.name: Schenner Waalweg
trails.why: The Schenna irrigation-channel path (Waalweg) runs through mixed woods and orchards from Verdins into the Naif valley.

trails.name: Percorso A Ovest del Cimone WS26
trails.why: The "Path of Wells and Mills" (WS26) from Ponte Sant'Anna, west of Monte Cimone.

trails.name: H03 - Al Passo - Bocchetta di Deccia
trails.why: Initially on a road then steep and tiring with a track often overrun by grasses, final stretch on stony ground and then on an exposed path, well paint marked

trails.name: Anello del Monte Muggio
trails.why: A loop around Monte Muggio over alpine pastures, past the small church of San Ulderico.

trails.name: Via Alpina Red R31

trails.name: D04 - Gabbio - Cima Lariè
trails.why: Historic paved mule track up to Monteossolano where the grape marc press is very interesting, then you climb up through traditional locality and high altitude pastures among larches and then the final ridge with vast panoramas

trails.name: Giro dei cinque laghi
trails.why: The "five lakes tour", walked clockwise.

trails.name: Cammino della Regina Camilla - Tappa 6
trails.why: A short stage from Giuliano di Roma to the village of Villa Santo Stefano.

trails.name: Sentiero dei Roccoli near Bergamo
trails.why: Wide views and a sunny slope that keeps this trail walkable even in winter.

trails.name: Strada Taverna
trails.why: An old trade and droving route that linked the valley with the main market towns all year round.

trails.name: F32 - Iselle - Alpe Pianezzoni
trails.why: From Iselle a short stretch of state road, then a path through the woods. Well marked and visible path. at times steep

trails.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 2A TAPPA Pian Cavallone - Monte Zeda - Bivacco Alpe Forna'
trails.why: Panoramic path along the ridge that from Pian Cavallone leads first to Pizzo Marona, then to Monte Zeda from which you descend the North ridge reserved for expert hikers and finally to the Alpe Forna' bivouac under the north face of Zeda

trails.name: Sentiero 6: La Strada Matrone
trails.why: Path no. 6 follows the old road built by the Matrone brothers up to the Great Cone of Vesuvius.

trails.name: Alta via n. 7 delle Dolomiti - I Tappa
trails.why: Alta Via 7, the "Alta Via di Patéra", is named after the Austrian climbing pioneer Lothar Patéra.

trails.name: G00 - Via del Gries da Riale a Passo del Gries (quarta sezione)
trails.why: From Riale to a little beyond Lake Morasco, proceed by road then begin the route on alpine paths passing through Bettelmat and then the steep climb that leads to Passo del Gries

trails.name: La Buca - Il Quartiere - Il Bottaccio - Passo di Cavorsella
trails.why: From La Buca, the path runs through woods and high meadows along the north side of Monte Cavalbianco, then up its west side past Bivacco Bottaccio to Punta Cavorsella.

trails.name: Sentiero Trekking Italia - Tappa 10
trails.why: A short final stage from Miranda to Isernia on back roads through fields and farms to a wide plain at the edge of the city.

trails.name: Anello del Monte Boral
trails.why: The Monte Boral loop, with a beautiful viewpoint over the whole Venetian plain and beyond.

trails.name: C07 - Seppiana - Alpe Zii - Alpe San Giacomo
trails.why: Path that from Seppiana, passing from the Alpe Zii and from the Colma lake cross, reaches the Alpe S. Giacomo and the oratory dedicated to the Saint.

trails.name: Great Crossing Elba South
trails.why: Part of the Alta Via della Valle d'Aosta, the high-level hiking route through the Aosta Valley.

trails.name: Alta Via delle Dolomiti n. 3 - VIII Tappa
trails.why: Alta Via 3 is a high route located in the Italian Dolomites between Niederdorf in the north and Longarone in the south.

trails.name: A24 - Alpe Marzone bivio A22 - Pizzo delle Pecore
trails.why: After a long walk on the road, you follow a shady ridge, then a long hillside towards Alpe Cort from which a steep path leads to the panoramic ridge and finally the summit

trails.name: Anello Campo - 3 Nordic Walking Park
trails.why: A trail of the Nordic Walking Park of Brenzone sul Garda.

trails.name: T24 - Laghetti di Nonio - Monte Novesso
trails.why: The route is mostly on forest roads. There are no signposts and few painted signs. The majestic beech tree "Fo' dl'umbrela" a few meters from the route is interesting.

trails.name: Alta Via n. 2 della Valle d'Aosta - Tappa 12
trails.why: Part of the Alta Via della Valle d'Aosta, the high-level hiking route through the Aosta Valley.

trails.name: Giro delle Teleferiche
trails.why: A route along the line of the heavy military cableway that linked Calliano station with Folgaria in the First World War.

trails.name: Sentiero Caracoli – Funtaneddi
trails.why: Monte San Calogero, the great massif above Termini Imerese, is named after the hermitage of San Calogero, whose ruins lie near the summit.

trails.name: Percorso ROSSO - Torri di Arcugnano
trails.why: A route for everyone and every season, following the cycle path from Torri di Arcugnano around Lake Fimon and back.

trails.name: T02 - Casale Corte Cerro - San Bartolomeo
trails.why: A path along the hillside with panoramic points over the lakes of Orta, Maggiore and Mergozzo.

trails.name: Sentiero delle Panchine
trails.why: The Benches Path at San Simone is a hiking route with six panoramic stops, each marked by a wooden bench.

trails.name: G31 - Lago Vannino - Bocchetta della Valle
trails.why: You go along the Vannino Lake then up to the beautiful prairies at the Busin Pass, a short hillside, danger of stones, with a wonderful view of Monte Giove and Lower Busin Lake, along the upper Busin Lake and with a short ascent the B.ta della Valle

trails.name: E50 - Piedicavallo - Colle della Vecchia
trails.why: The route winds along an ancient paved mule track, and features writings and drawings made by professional stonemasons at the time of construction commissioned by the patron Federico Rosazza in 1876.

trails.name: H10 - Alpe Devero - Diga di Agaro
trails.why: Interesting route: the waterfalls of the Devero stream, vast panoramas of the mountains surrounding the Devero from Cistella to Pizzo Crampiolo, arrival in a dive on Lake Agaro

trails.name: Sopra la Valle dell'Orco
trails.why: The route passes several hamlets whose different buildings and materials show the typical architecture of the area and the way people lived.

trails.name: Strada delle 52 gallerie
trails.why: The Strada delle 52 Gallerie, also known as the 52 Tunnel Road, or Strada della Prima Armata is a military mule road built during World War I on the Pasubio massif in Veneto, Italy.

trails.name: Sentiero Natura del Castello
trails.why: A walk around the remains of an ancient castle on the Bregonze hills, about an hour and a half with a modest 160 m climb.

trails.name: Alta Via dei Monti Lattari - 01
trails.why: The first part of the Alta Via dei Monti Lattari, which runs from Cava de' Tirreni to Punta Campanella.

trails.name: S02 Cannobio - San Bartolomeo Valmara
trails.why: From Cannobio to San Bartolomeo Valmara, walking first on the long lake of Lido di Cannobio and then on the "Via delle Genti" through Campeglio, Cinzago, San Bartolomeo in Montibus with its beautiful ancient church of Romanesque origin, Formine.

trails.name: G00 - Via del Gries da Ponte a Riale (terza sezione)
trails.why: Path in an alpine environment of Walser culture. Spectacular view of the Toce waterfall

trails.name: Ardito Desio
trails.why: CAI trail 642, dedicated to the geologist and explorer Ardito Desio.

trails.name: B401 - Oliena - Monte Corrasi
trails.why: As for F401 that goes up from the base to Mount Limbara, those who go up to Mount Corrasi from Oliena do so to climb it in its entirety, better by car in Tuones.

trails.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 4A TAPPA da Bivacco Lidesh a Bivacco Scaredi
trails.why: One of the most challenging stages of the Bove trail, the ascent to the Torrione on the Passo delle Crocette side is mountaineering and facilitated by chains, the ascent on the Bocchetta di Terza side is all on a trail with very exposed sections

trails.name: Sentiero Case la Pazza – Piano Pomo – Piano Sempria
trails.why: A trail past the many "màrcati", old shepherds' enclosures of the Madonie.

trails.name: R05 Caprezzo - Pian Cavallone bivio R07
trails.why: The route connects Caprezzo to the R07 crossroads just below the CAI refuge at Pian Cavallone.

trails.name: F50b - Ciamporino - Alpe Solcio
trails.why: Superb panoramic half mountainside route, along the path of Alta Via Val Divedro, along pastures still loaded for grazing of cattle with refurbished huts for holiday use where the original features have been maintained.

trails.name: A52 - Mergozzo - Bracchio - Vercio - Monte Faiè
trails.why: From Mergozzo lake to Monte Faiè the initial chestnut trees give way up to the beech trees while you gain altitude on the ancient cobbled mule track to the Vercio Hermitage and then on to the ridge with breathtaking views of the Gulf Borromeo and Stresa

trails.name: Cammino della Regina Camilla - Tappa 5
trails.why: A short stage from Prossedi to the village of Giuliano di Roma.

trails.name: Lungo l'Acquasaliente
trails.why: The route climbs the Acquasaliente valley, at times along the stream, showing how place names reflect the land, its crops and its legends.

trails.name: H09 - Cravegna - Alpe Agarù. Parte della Veia di Scuettar
trails.why: The Veia di Scuettar or Via degli Scoiattoli was once traveled with herds by the inhabitants of Crodo to reach Alpe Devero along a hillside route.

trails.name: Valle delle Prigioni
trails.why: The route passes through a narrow tunnel about ten metres long that carries an aqueduct.

trails.name: Sentiero 2 - Anello dei Bollori
trails.why: Roundtrip part of Via Francigena and Francigena Mare, passing through the cave "Grotta alla Vacca" and the thermal spring "I Bollori".

trails.name: Tossicia - Colle Cennone
trails.region: Club Alpino Italiano, Sezione di Teramo
trails.why: A vigorous hike on trails and forest roads, through beautiful woods, past the hidden church of Sant'Andrea and the small village of Flamignano, up Colle Cennone and ending with beautiful views of the mountains and the Teramo area.

trails.name: Sentiero dei Ponti
trails.why: A route through the lower part of Corna Imagna across three old stone bridges.

trails.name: Tappa 2 - Da Vinci a Mignana
trails.why: Second leg from Vinci to Mignana, where where you join the path 10A to Pietramarina, archeological area where in the past was an etruscan fortification.

trails.name: P02 - Cossogno - Pizzo Pernice
trails.why: From Cossogno amidst chestnut on the ancient cobbled mule track to Alpe Rugno, then for the meadows of high pastures and finally the long panoramic ridge that culminates at Pizzo Pernice

trails.name: Confinale
trails.why: Along the Swiss border, past many boundary stones set by the army engineers in the early 1900s.

trails.name: M37 - Villette - Bocchetta di Sant'Antonio
trails.why: An interesting path between larch groves and blueberry meadows following the ancient mule track on which the wealthy lords of the belle epoque went to the thermal baths of Bagni di Craveggia

trails.name: A38 - Premosello - Bocchetta di Saler
trails.why: Long and tiring path. It is possible to reduce the height difference by driving up to Colloro.

trails.name: H16 - Crampiolo - Passo del Muretto
trails.why: Starting in Crampiolo, reachable from Alpe Devero, well signposted, it runs through larch woods up to Alpe Sangiatto, then on high altitude meadows, passes the B.ta di Scarpia, descends to Alpe Pojala, climbs another hill and arrives at the Muretto Pass

trails.name: Percorso della Memoria near Ponte di Legno
trails.why: A path of about 5.5 km from the Bettolino picnic area to the Doss de l'Ora along an old military mule track.

trails.name: G07 - Crodo - Passo della Colmine
trails.why: From Crodo to Viceno a nice mule track, crossing several agglomerations. From Viceno to Foppiano the route is no longer marked and in some places difficult to find.

trails.name: F28 - Alpe Veglia - Bocchetta di Aurona
trails.why: Very dangerous path for falling rocks in the final part, where the glacier of Aurona disappeared, equipped with chains and pegs fixed in the rock.

trails.name: P40 - Alpe in La Piana - Alpe della Colma
trails.why: Final path of the classic North South crossing of the wild Valgrande for a route easy to follow and maintained by the Ente Parco Valgrande

trails.name: Anello Cascata del Bognon
trails.why: The Bognon waterfall loop, a not too demanding walk in the wild upper Val Brenta.

trails.name: Traccia Partigiana

trails.name: M02 - Marone - Pizzo Marcio
trails.why: Long and tiring route, long unmarked stretches, track sometimes difficult to find and missing in the valley after Sassoledo where there is an elementary rocky jump.

trails.name: Sentiero 34 della Val Bona
trails.why: From Val Biandino to Rifugio Grassi over the Bocchetta di Valbona.

trails.name: Variante Spina
trails.why: A link from path 300 directly to Termini, part of the Alta Via, avoiding the rough stretch via Recommone.

trails.name: Le Vie del Verde (Itinerario 2)
trails.why: A spring walk on the hills of Bergamo's Città Alta, along a long green way past some of the city's most beautiful places.

trails.name: Anello del Gamonda
trails.why: A loop of Monte Gamonda, little known for its modest height but unusual for the sheer drop on one side.

trails.name: S17 Falmenta - Cresta est Monte Vadà bivio R19
trails.why: From Falmenta go down on asphalted road to the bridge over the Falmenta stream, after the path go up to the right to the Monti Barro and Ortighedo, then always on the N-E ridge of Monte Vadà and with a traverse reach the crossroads R19 on the east ridge.

trails.name: Passo del Melancoro - Serra Comune - Pizzo Deta
trails.why: A ridge trail from the Passo del Melancoro over Serra Comune to Pizzo Deta.

trails.name: G17 - Premia - La Pioda
trails.why: Initially gentle path on the meadows of Altoggio then from the Madonna dell'Oro it climbs with a long stairway up to the upper edge of precipices which it runs along until its end near a beautiful waterfall

trails.name: D99 - Bivio D08 - Passo di Variola
trails.why: A low route for the Variola pass, the route, almost entirely on the hillside, follows the course of the Variola stream through the Dorca and Variola mountain pastures to lead to the pass of the same name

trails.name: Sentiero Naturalistico dello Spaccasassi
trails.why: The Canzo - Prim'Alpe - Canzo loop, about 3.5 hours and demanding, with 11 panels on flora, fauna, geology and landscape.

trails.name: Via Abati Variante Farini
trails.why: The Via degli Abati is a pilgrim way from Pavia to Bobbio and on through Bardi and Borgo Val di Taro to Pontremoli.

trails.name: Anello dell'Orello
trails.why: From Via Capo ai Pini along a firebreak ridge with a view over the whole of Lacona.

trails.name: B485 - Ponte S'Abba Arva - Gola di Gorropu
trails.why: An easy path to the famous Gorropu Canyon, also suitable for tourists with some walking experience.

trails.name: Sentiero degli Alpini near Bassano del Grappa
trails.region: Club Alpino Italiano sezione di Thiene
trails.why: The Strada degli Alpini, from Arsiero to Monte Cimone, was built in 1909 by Alpine troops on the western side of the mountain.

trails.name: P30 - Alpe in La Piana - Alpe Scaredi
trails.why: One of the pats of the classic North South crossing of the wild Valgrande for a route easy to follow and maintained by the Ente Parco Valgrande

trails.name: Giro delle contrade di Fondra
trails.why: The "Giro delle Contrade" follows old mule tracks to the historic hamlets of Isola di Fondra on the slopes of Monte Torcola.

trails.name: S12 Orasso - Bugnago - Spoccia
trails.why: High route between Orasso and Spoccia through the terraces and high mountain pastures of the two villages: Bugnago, Ghilone, Niva and Cheibi.

trails.name: Mulattiera Orsano-Megano
trails.why: The path follows the old mule track from Orsano to Megano and the Sant'Erasmo uplands.

trails.name: Sentiere delle Marocche
trails.why: A walk through rock debris looking for dinosaur footprints, ideal in early spring, through a special biotope to the lake of Cavedine.

trails.name: D19 - bivio D20 presso Picciola - Passo del Fornalino
trails.why: Route for the Fornalino pass and the Antrona Valley, steep at times and exposed, poor signposts

trails.name: P12 - Pogallo - Bocchetta di Terza
trails.why: From Val Pogallo to Val Cannobina, crossing the ridge where the Bove path runs. This was also the route of the partisans fleeing to Switzerland during the German-Fascist raid of 1944

trails.name: Sentiero Life delle Alpi Retiche – Dal cigno alla pernice bianca
trails.why: A route through 5 protected nature sites, for experienced hikers, with protected passages.

trails.name: Via Francigena - Variant stream Valchetta
trails.why: The Via Francigena is an ancient road and pilgrimage route running from the cathedral city of Canterbury in England, through France and Switzerland, to Rome and then to Apulia, where there were the ports of embarkation for the Holy Land.

trails.name: Itinerarium Rosaliae - Tappa 1B
trails.why: A short, beautiful stage from the hermitage of the Quisquina, with the cave where Santa Rosalia is said to have lived, to Santo Stefano Quisquina.

trails.name: Sentiero 4 - Anello delle Carbonaie
trails.why: Roundtrip part of Francigena Mare with connection to "Sentiero 3 - Anello delle due Vie", passing through the thermal spring "I Bollori".

trails.name: Sentiero 5: Il Gran Cono
trails.why: Nature path no. 5, "Il Gran Cono", leads to the crater of Vesuvius from the car park at 1,000 m.

trails.name: Itinerario 11
trails.why: A medium-length route with little climbing between Casere dei Boschi and the top of Monte Avena.

trails.name: P08 - Cicogna -Tregugno - la Soliva - Pian Cavallone
trails.why: A challenging path for complexity, development and difficulty, the path from la Soliva to the Forcola Saddle is on steep meadows and You crosse a valley with vertical rocky walls supported by the chains

trails.name: P01 - Madonna di campagna - Monterosso - Cavandone
trails.why: An easy walk on Monterosso, mountain overlooking Verbania. Roads and firebreaks facilitate the journey.

trails.name: R15 Aurano - Calpera - il Colle
trails.why: The route connects Aurano passing through its numerous ancient Courts and Pastures to il Colle, a crossroads of numerous other routes coming from all directions.

trails.name: C12 - Viganella - Alpe Barco - Alpe Cavallo
trails.why: This is, of the three possible, the longest and most demanding route to reach the Alpe Cavallo

trails.name: H11 - Alpe Devero - Monte Cazzola
trails.why: The route begins in a larch forest to Alpe Misanco; beyond this point, the vegetation thins out and eventually disappears, and the path continues through an almost lunar landscape to the Buscagna Lakes and, finally, to our destination.

trails.name: R06 Trobaso - Pian Nava
trails.why: From Trobaso in Verbania past Possaccio, old terraces, Cà di Müii and the Sentiero delle Coppelle with its rock engravings.

trails.name: A54 - Bracchio - Cappella di Erfo - Monte Faiè
trails.why: From Lake Mergozzo, Bracchio fraction, through Alpe Boscopiano and Alpe Ompio with the Refuge Fantoli up to 1352 meters of Mount Faiè.

trails.name: Sentiero 3 - Anello delle due Vie
trails.why: Roundtrip part of Via Francigena and Francigena Mare, passing through the cave "Grotta alla Vacca" and the thermal spring "I Bollori".

trails.name: Sentiero del Partigiano Angelo Gotti
trails.why: The route of the young partisan courier Angelo Gotti of the Fiamme Verdi, captured and killed at Cascina Como.

trails.name: Sentiero della Cultura Casearia near Varenna
trails.region: GAL Valle Brembana e Sezione CAI di Bergamo
trails.why: A short loop on paths and mule tracks through the hamlets of the Val Taleggio and their typical architecture, for every walker.

trails.name: Via di Linari - tappa 8 - Rigoso - Linari (ruderi)
trails.why: The Via di Linari is an ancient route of commercial passage and pilgrimage to Rome as an alternative to the Via Francigena on which it was grafted from the city of Fidenza towards Parma to reach Tuscany through the Lagastrello Pass

trails.name: Sentiero 5 - Anello di Maurizio
trails.why: A round trip to the Grotte di Maurizio caves, the Acquedotto della Forra aqueduct and Poggio alla Forra.

trails.name: P09 - Cicogna - Ponte Velina
trails.why: Between ancient summer pastures and centuries-old chestnut to explore the southern part of the National Park to reach the last inhabited permanently pasture of the Val Grande

trails.name: Sentiero Partigiano Ercole Pedretti
trails.why: A little-used trail, a fine alternative to the classic routes to the Laghi Gemelli.

trails.name: P11 - Cicogna - Cima Sasso
trails.why: Panoramic ridge path between Val Pogallo and Val Grande, easy until the Casa dell'Alpino, some little difficulty the final climb to the top

trails.name: Percorso dello Scoiattolo
trails.why: A themed walk about the history of cherry growing in this area.

trails.name: Sentiero del Castagno near Bellagio
trails.why: The Sentiero del Castagno is a loop through the history of Corna Imagna and its chestnut groves.

trails.name: Le Vie del Verde (Itinerario 1)
trails.why: A spring walk on the hills of Bergamo's Città Alta, along a long green way past some of the city's most beautiful places.

trails.name: Sojo Negro
trails.why: The path is named after an outcrop of volcanic rock along its first part.

trails.name: Sentiero Nociazzi
trails.why: A magnificent but demanding walk from the hamlet of Nociazzi near Castellana Sicula.

trails.name: R01 Verbania Trobaso - Unchio - Motto di Unchio - Pian di Les - Cossogno
trails.why: From Verbania Trobaso, Via al Cotonificio, you reach the cycle road on the left side of the San Bernardino river, go up to Unchio and the Oratory of Motto di Unchio, then through a peat bog and Pian di Les, you reach Cossogno.

trails.name: Sentiero Alminusa (Favara e Granza)
trails.why: An old sandstone-paved mule track from near Aliminusa into the Bosco del Cardellino, over the Passo Scacciavalloni.

trails.name: G18 - Canza - Bta di Tamia
trails.why: Up to Alpe Tamia suitable for mountain hikers, after Alpe Tamia for the difficulty of finding the route due to the lack of track and trail signs and for the exposure on the final bare rock, it is reserved for experts

trails.name: Itinerario 14
trails.why: A new route into the heart of the Massa Lubrense countryside, between Massa and Sant'Agata on the Sorrento peninsula.

trails.name: Sentiero della Cultura Casearia near Sondrio
trails.region: GAL Valle Brembana e Sezione CAI di Bergamo
trails.why: Up the mule track still used to bring the cattle to the high pastures, a little-known way into one of the busiest corners of the Orobie.

trails.name: S21 Gurro loc. Tresco, bivio S01 - La Piota
trails.why: From Tresco above Gurro, crossroads with S01 and GTA, climb to the top of la Piota where you reach the Sentiero Bove.

trails.name: VE1 - Invorio - Bocchetta Borsaga
trails.why: Path eroded by water, practically not signposted, sections invaded by vegetation. At the beginning of the climb you pass as if you were in the bed of a small stream with rocky jumps.

trails.name: C32 - Forcola di Cheggio
trails.why: Panoramic route that connects the Troncone Valley with the Loranco Valley through the Forcola pass and its mountain pastures

trails.name: Z05 - Sambughetto - Massa del Turlo
trails.why: A very steep climb up to Colle del Campo then the easy and panoramic ridge to follow up to the summit

trails.name: F50 - Alpe Veglia - Ciamporino
trails.why: From the Rifugio CAI Città di Arona a path in a larch wood leads first to the Alpe La Balma and then to the "Portea".

trails.name: Il Sentiero dell'Ariosto
trails.why: Dedicated to the poet Ludovico Ariosto, who lived in Castelnuovo di Garfagnana from 1522 to 1525 as ducal governor of the Garfagnana for the Este dukes.

trails.name: P14 - Pogallo - Cima Marsicce
trails.why: A magnificent panoramic path with breathtaking views of the ridges of the BOVE trail, elementary but tiring to the Alpe Busarasca, the long final crest is reserved for hikers specially experienced

trails.name: percorso comunale 5
trails.why: From the Sestola riding stables to the church of San Giovanni Battista in Roncoscaglia.

trails.name: A58 - Mergozzo - Linea Cadorna - Mont'Orfano vetta
trails.why: The A56 and A58 trails with Mont'Orfano ring, rich in historical points of interest: the granite quarries and military works of the Cadorna Line, and landscaping with 360 views over Lake Maggiore and Orta, and the peaks of the Val Grande to the Mottarone

trails.name: G14 - Foppiano - Alpe Cramec
trails.why: Path that from Foppiano leads to Alpe Cramec and the homonymous lake, through Alpe Croce

trails.name: Il Cammino del Gran Sasso - Tappa 3
trails.why: A short, easy stage from Rocca di Calascio to Santo Stefano di Sessanio, full of sights and suitable for families with children.

trails.name: A56 - Mergozzo - Sentiero Azzurro - Mont'Orfano vetta
trails.why: The A56 and A58 trails with Mont'Orfano ring, rich in historical points of interest: the granite quarries and military works of the Cadorna Line, and landscaping with 360 views over Lake Maggiore and Orta, and the peaks of the Val Grande to the Mottarone

trails.name: Sentiero della Scala Santa
trails.why: A loop from Santa Libera that crosses the Rio Chiappea ravine on a bold footbridge and the legendary Scala Santa to the lonely chapel of San Bovo, with a superb view over the Belbo valley.

trails.name: Bagatti Gelsi Villoresi
trails.region: Parco Grubrìa - Comune di Paderno Dugnano, Comune di Nova Milanese, Comune di Varedo
trails.why: From Viale Bagatti to Grugnotorto via the Oasi dei Gelsi and the Villoresi canal towpath.

trails.name: Alta via n. 7 delle Dolomiti - III Tappa
trails.why: Alta Via 7, the "Alta Via di Patéra", is named after the Austrian climbing pioneer Lothar Patéra.

trails.name: R07 Intragna - Cappella del Pian Cavallone
trails.why: In very open environment between Intragna and the Rifugio Pian Cavallone CAI Verbano,through Cambiesso and Sunfaì along the route of the Valle Intrasca Marathon.

trails.name: Sentiero della Madonna del Monte
trails.why: Lower part on steep roads then a crooked mule track then a stretch on asphalt then dirt road and path overgrown with brambles then difficult to follow but at the top it improves in a beech forest

trails.name: B162 - Parcheggio Fuili - Cala Luna
trails.why: The path winds through the Mediterranean scrub overlooking the coast, it has some ups and downs, the bottom is on limestone rock for a long time and care is required especially if wet, Cala Luna is a little gem to see

trails.name: VM2 - Baveno - Alpe Vedabia
trails.why: Initially you travel along roads and dirt roads till Romanico then you enter broad-leaved woods up to the destination with a route mainly on paths and forest tracks.

trails.name: Percorso ARANCIO - Lago Alto
trails.why: From the second landing stage, a level circuit of Lake Fimon along the higher, more panoramic Pianezze shore.

trails.name: La Via Decia - Via Breve
trails.region: Club Alpino Italiano - Sottosezione Val di Scalve
trails.why: The Via Breve is a three-day alternative to the five-day La Via Decia.

trails.name: F03 - Alpe Salviggia - Lorino
trails.why: Until Prato Grande, in the woods, well kept. From Pratogrande to Crucible 1524, very steep and quite clean.

trails.name: L'Eremo - Campo Pianelli - Pietra di Bismantova - L'Eremo
trails.why: A loop around and onto the Pietra di Bismantova: along its east base, round the wooded north side and up to the summit plateau, then down the west side.

trails.name: Percorso della Memoria near Florence
trails.why: A 5 km memorial loop through the places of the 1944 massacre of the Einstein family at Rignano.

trails.name: Forca di Valle - Colle Pelato
trails.region: Club Alpino Italiano, Sezione di Teramo
trails.why: Mountain walk on paths and country tracks crossing meadows and forest to the top of the Colle Pelato.

trails.name: C03 - Collegamento Gran Anello Ovest
trails.why: Connection route between the Anello del Tartufo and Anello dei Castelli.

trails.name: G30 - Cagiogno - Aleccio
trails.why: From Cagiogno, by mule track, to the beautiful Bee mountain pasture from which, by a path that is exposed at times on the hillside, you reach the Aloro mountain pasture.

trails.name: Magna Via Francigena: Variante tappa 1
trails.why: A variant for those who want to avoid the many kilometres of asphalt on the first stage.

trails.name: A34 - Vogogna - Pizzo Lacina
trails.why: Very steep and tiring route reserved for expert hikers, the final part is an extremely panoramic ridge over the whole of Ossola

trails.name: G00a - Montecrestese - Pontemaglio
trails.why: Once a trade route for mule caravans between Switzerland and Italy and called Via dello Sbrinz.

trails.name: Sentiero Carandi
trails.why: A loop through the green countryside and soft hills of Ceresole d'Alba, past the hamlet of Carandi.

trails.name: SENTIERO BOVE - 3A TAPPA da Bivacco Alpe Forna' a Bivacco Lidesh
trails.why: Panoramic ridge easy path but still very exposed trail. From altitude 1873, after Piota and before Cima Crocette, a possible escape route to the Pian di Boit bivouac is possible on easy meadows without trail

trails.name: C05 - Seppiana - Alpe S. Giacomo
trails.why: The route from Seppiana reaches, passing through the mountain pastures of Crotto, Mandariola and Baldana, the Alpe S. Giacomo and the oratory dedicated to the Saint.

trails.name: A28 - Prata - Pizzo Lacina
trails.why: Steep and tiring route with very difficult sections to follow, the final part is on extremely steep and trackless meadows.

trails.name: A32 - Vogogna - Alpe Ceresola - bivio A28
trails.why: Steep and tiring route reserved for capable hikers, the final part is an extremely panoramic ridge over the north Ossola

trails.name: Valbona e Valmara
trails.why: Valbona and Valmara are the two main valleys of Santa Caterina: one gentle, farmed and settled, the other steep but rich in water, with several mills.

trails.name: T702 - Bruncu Spina - Punta La Marmora
trails.why: The route follows a hillside path to the Arcu Gennargentu saddle, with a very steep and slippery final section, then a scenic ridge to the summit.

trails.name: A26 - Cuzzego località Carale - bivio A24 Pizzo Colla Bassa
trails.why: Tiring and steep path at times made impassable by falling trees, track often not visible, very poor marked, steep and exposed meadows in the upper part

trails.name: Sentiero dei Borghi
trails.why: A 5 km loop through medieval Roncola.

trails.name: F01b - S. Giovanni - Alpe Bogo
trails.why: beginning of the high route of the Divedro valley. Panoramic trail with well-kept mountain pastures.

trails.name: D06 - Costa d'Agrello
trails.why: Long route in an isolated environment, through woods and ridges that are not very exposed and not very frequented

trails.name: Sentiero Vallone dei Molini (San Mauro Castelverde)
trails.why: The Vallone dei Molini, named after its many old watermills, winds through lush vegetation along the Giardinello stream.

trails.name: Alta Via n. 1 della Valle d'Aosta - Tappa 13
trails.why: Part of the Alta Via della Valle d'Aosta, the high-level hiking route through the Aosta Valley.

trails.name: Aquilano - Selva degli Abeti
trails.why: Forest walk on footpaths and forest tracks to the Selva degli Abeti.

trails.name: La Via della Neve
trails.why: The route links Passiano, near Cava de' Tirreni, with the summit of Monte Sant'Angelo and the Alta Via dei Monti Lattari.

trails.name: Direttissima Crocetta
trails.why: Wonderful path up to the peak. Some parts are very steep and path is not always easy to find.

trails.name: A08 - Masera località Ranco - Alpe Pescia
trails.why: Along the ancient mule track of ascent to the mountain pastures. Very scenic route on the Ossolana plain.

trails.name: Sentiero delle Formichelle
trails.why: The Sentiero delle Formichelle is an old footpath linking Tramonti with the seaside towns of Maiori and Minori.

trails.name: R08 Aurano - Esio - Premeno
trails.why: The route starts from Aurano, descends to the stream of Val Luisina crossing the provincial road several times; it climbs to Esio with a path immersed in broadleaf forest and first on the road and then on a comfortable mule track comes to Premeno.

trails.name: D14 - Gomba - Passo di Oriaccia
trails.why: Initially steep route follows the final stretch of the Vertical "La Veia" from Alpe Dente becomes a pleasant panoramic path halfway up the hill towards Lake Oriaccia a short stretch on a rocky slope leads to the pass.

trails.name: Sentiero di Santa Maria ai Monti
trails.why: A link between Ravello and the high path of the Valle delle Ferriere, passing Santa Maria dei Monti, one of the best-known shrines of the area.

trails.name: Latschenweg - Sentiero Pino Mugo
trails.why: The Latschenkiefernweg on the Villanderer Alm, with a unique panorama all the way.

trails.name: La Via dell'Acqua
trails.why: A quiet walk along the Leogra river, through fine scenery and historic and cultural sights.

trails.name: S07 Sant'Anna (Traffiume) - Pro Redond
trails.why: From the Orrido of S.Anna in Traffiume, after passing the SP 75, go up a steep mule track to I Pianoni, take the left and pass the Rio Barala, go up to Alpe Gallona and reach Pro Redond, a wonderful balcony overlooking the northern part of Lake Maggiore.

trails.name: F06 - Varzo - Alpe Solcio
trails.why: Well marked trail with several passages next to the road, does not present difficulties

trails.name: T20b - Bivio T22 - Alpe Camasca
trails.why: Path that takes place entirely on a dirt road that is very practicable and used by mountain bikes.

trails.name: F99 - Alpe Veglia - Passo di Valtendra
trails.why: Beautiful walk in the larch woods up to Pian du Scricc then go up to Pian Sass Mor where appear the steep rampart that precedes the Valtendra Pass, years ago covered by perennial snowfield and now land without vegetation

trails.name: G21 - Passo - Salecchio Superiore
trails.why: Easy and profitable route that reaches the Walser settlement of Salecchio, an unlit tunnel is easily circumvented with a marked route

trails.name: G19 - San Rocco - Casarola di sopra
trails.why: Very steep and tiring path with a thin and sometimes non-existent track in the upper part

trails.name: Brunate-Montepiatto
trails.region: Gruppo Volontari per la Protezione Ambientale di Blevio
trails.why: A panoramic route through the woods above Blevio, linking the "Monti", the old farming hamlets on the slope above Lake Como.

trails.name: H14 - Lago di Devero - Bocchetta della Valle
trails.why: From the H98 you go up into a larch forest coming out to the Alpe della Valle, then to the Alpe Naga and at the crossroads with H08 which goes up to the Pojala Pass you head to the left and proceeding halfway up the hill you reach at the B.ta della Valle

trails.name: D13 - Bognanco - Pioi
trails.why: A route that is exposed in parts and leads from Bognanco to Pioi. The route is of particular interest for those who want to travel along the lower valley following the two banks as part of a circular valley itinerary.

trails.name: D18 - Bivio D98 presso Alpe Vallaro - Passo di Pontimia
trails.why: Route in the uncontaminated territories of the upper valley, you travel three passes and meet the Campo lakes to find yourself on the border in front of the Waissmiess

trails.name: Martinsweg
trails.why: Family adventure trails in Marling: a forest trail with a rope course and a nature trail.

trails.name: Prati di S. Rocco
trails.why: Meadows and pastures shape San Rocco and this route, with many traces of old farming terraces.

trails.name: Valle del Brunone Percorso C
trails.why: Nature walks in the Valle del Brunone above Berbenno, a natural monument and a fossil site of world importance.

trails.name: G12 - Passo - Alpe Groppo
trails.why: Very steep and tiring path with a track beyond Pianezza di sopra overgrown with vegetation and GPS needed to find it

trails.name: Percorso dei prati magri
trails.region: Parco Regionale di Montevecchia e della Valle del Curone
trails.why: A walk of about 2.5 km, an hour and a half, to the fascinating petrifying springs; hiking boots recommended.

trails.name: Santa Caterinella
trails.why: The path is named after the votive chapel of Santa Caterinella, which recalls an event and a miracle.

trails.name: B38 - Bivio B45 - Capanna Eugenio Sella
trails.why: A challenging and panoramic route on the east face of Monte Rosa that leads to the former refuge, now the Bivacco Sella, and to the crossroads for the Iacchini Pass or the Bocchetta Stenigalchi.

trails.name: Alta Via n. 1 della Valle d'Aosta - Tappa 9
trails.why: Part of the Alta Via della Valle d'Aosta, the high-level hiking route through the Aosta Valley.

trails.name: M35 - Zornasco - Alpe Fontana Verde
trails.why: Initially very steep path once you reach the ridge follow it with easier slopes. A small stretch at altitude 1147 on a steep slope on the north side requires attention.

trails.name: B481 - Ponte S'Abba Arva - Tiscali
trails.why: Shady and well-marked path to reach Tiscali, a very short final stretch of rocky and sometimes exposed path is reserved for expert hikers

trails.name: via ferrata "Sentiero Corbellini"
trails.why: The Sentiero Corbellini via ferrata, part of trail 316 to Sappada.

trails.name: Terre e miniere
trails.why: The mountainside holds materials mined by people over time, such as silver, kaolin and quartzite; the route passes several of these sites, especially the kaolin quarry area.

trails.name: G41 - Bettelmat - Lago dei Sabbioni
trails.why: A very popular route that starts from the Bettelmatt mountain pasture, famous for its cheeses, passes through the Rif.

trails.name: P06 - Cicogna - Varola - Curgei - Pizzo Pernice
trails.why: Tough route for steep slopes to go up, but no technical difficulty, even marks, albeit sometimes distant, are present throughout the path and the trace is always visible

trails.name: R03a Cappella Fina bivio R03 - Bivio R05 tra Cappella Porta e Cornala
trails.why: Connection route between Cappella Fina and crossroads with R05 Cappella Porta-Cornala. Useful for the R03-R05 ring route through Pian Cavallone.

trails.name: C05 - Collegamento Paesante
trails.why: Connection route between the Anello dei Castelli and the historic center of San Miniato.

trails.name: Via Abati Variante Caffaraccia
trails.why: The Via degli Abati is a pilgrim way from Pavia to Bobbio and on through Bardi and Borgo Val di Taro to Pontremoli.

trails.name: D15 - Picciola bivio D19 - Bivio C06
trails.why: A short stretch among beech woods leads us to Curtit where there is an ancient mine. Among meadows and high altitude pastures we reach the Scatta locality from here, halfway up the hill, we reach the Saudera locality and shortly after the C06 path

trails.name: S08 Cavaglio - Monte Giove
trails.why: From Cavaglio San Donnino go along the Rio Cavaglio valley and cross it on the Ganna bridge, go up to the mountain pastures Cruscina and Biessen to reach Alpe Rombiago and from here to the nearby top of the Monte Giove.

trails.name: B33 - Parte verso Macugnaga del Sentiero Genoni
trails.why: Route reserved for expert hikers with often uneven and disused tracks. Final section with small climbing sections made easier by the presence of well-maintained safety ropes.

trails.name: H06 - Croveo - Diga di Agaro
trails.why: Interesting very scenic route on the ancient mule track that went up to the Walser village of Agaro now submerged by the lake.

trails.name: Naturalistico di Parè
trails.why: A mostly flat loop around the hill above Colombirolo, with geology, plants and wildlife along the way.

trails.name: R07a Cambiesso - Cappella Porta
trails.why: From Cambiesso to Cappella Porta passing by Corte Steppio, still loaded with animals in summer and with some well-kept huts, and then by the old pastures of Pechi-Campale, Gajin and Fai.

trails.name: G10 - San Rocco - Alpe Groppo
trails.why: Very steep and tiring path with a thin and sometimes non-existent track in the upper part.

trails.name: R14 Aurano - Luera
trails.why: The route starts from Aurano, crosses some little valleys to reach the Alpe Erbia and then, with a flat path, reaches Luera, crossroads the R10, R12, R18, R22 routes.

trails.name: A51 - Cimamulera - Pizzo Castello
trails.why: Service trail to the pastures of the South/East side of Pizzo Castello with panoramic views over the valleys, the junction with C07 connects the Colma and S. Giacomo mountain pastures

trails.name: Sentiero dell'Acqua near Bergamo
trails.why: A walk through the centre of the village to La Canal, an old spring of pure, excellent water.

trails.name: R36 Fudrasca - Monte Pian Bello
trails.why: From the junction with R20 to Fudrasca, towards Piazza, near the Oratory of Sant'Eurosia of the XVII century, then towards Colle Pianbello to finish on Mount Pianbello to the R38.

trails.name: Sentiero di Villa Notari
trails.why: The path starts in the chestnut woods on the slopes of Monte Faito, at Campetiello, first on a winding gravel road.

trails.name: C96 - Prato - Alpe Colma dei Prei
trails.why: This route, from Prato to Colma dei Prei, is part of the GTA stage that from Antrona, loc.ty Cheggio arrives precisely at the refuge of Colma.

trails.name: C01 - Villadossola-Alpe Baldana bivio C05
trails.why: Route from Villadossola, through the fractions of Piaggio Sopra and Gaggitti, going up, passing through the pastures of Corticcio, Basciumo Sotto and Sopra, reaches the Baldana alp.

trails.name: X14 - Alpe Busarasca - Bocchetta di Campo
trails.why: A wild path in one of the most remote areas of Val Pogallo, following a non-existent track, looking for obligatory passages, walking on very steep meadows are a constant throughout the entire route

trails.name: Giro del Pizzo di Cusio
trails.why: A beautiful loop around the Pizzo di Cusio.

trails.name: S14 Orasso - Alpe Pluni
trails.why: From Orasso to Alpe Pluni via Monte Vecchio, over the pass on the south-west slopes of Monte Torriggia.

trails.name: Sentiero dei Castagneti di Tavernate
trails.why: The route links Amalfi with the village of Pogerola and its woods, known for their chestnut groves.

trails.name: F22 - Alpe Veglia - Lago Bianco - Passo di Boccareccio
trails.why: steep and difficult path, up to Lago Bianco, 2160 m; quiet from the lake to Pian d'Erbioi 2300 m. then last stretch very steep, tiring, on an impervious path

trails.name: Sentiero Zappino
trails.why: The Zappino path links the top of the Pino hill, at 575 m, with the edge of Pimonte.

trails.name: B505 - Ghenna Silana - Gorropu
trails.why: The descent to the Gorropu Gorge is also an interesting excursion in a large forest of centuries-old holm oaks, one of which and a strawberry tree are registered in the monumental tree register.

trails.name: Itinerario fuoriporta 1 - Moscosa
trails.why: An easy walk for all ages to discover the natural beauty around Amandola.

trails.name: Anello dei tre campanili
trails.why: A loop through the parish churches of Zelbio, Veleso and Erno.

trails.name: Via Francigena - Variant of the Camillaro bridge
trails.why: The Via Francigena is an ancient road and pilgrimage route running from the cathedral city of Canterbury in England, through France and Switzerland, to Rome and then to Apulia, where there were the ports of embarkation for the Holy Land.

trails.name: Sentiero Stagno Gorgonero – Piano Catarineci
trails.why: Through the Vallone Scopalacqua, with a stop at the spring.

trails.name: S09 Bivio S11 sopra Socraggio - Bocchetta del Tondone
trails.why: From the crossroads above Socraggio up to the Piazzola and Aurasco alps, then to the Monti Sommalemna and the Bocchetta del Tondone.

trails.name: D13 - Delubro - Oropa Sport
trails.why: Initially on a dirt road recently widened to 4 m except for the initial stretch then on a paved mule track

trails.name: Grand Tour del Lago Maggiore ® - Tappa 7 - Variante alta Colmegna - Maccagno
trails.why: An 11-stage trek that brings together and connects ancient historical routes, paths and pre-existing trails on the shores and hills surrounding Lake Maggiore, designed by CAI Sezione Verbano Intra.

trails.name: H04 - Croveo - Diga di Agaro
trails.why: Path for experts has some sections with chains and often strong exposure

trails.name: Strada Tedesca
trails.why: Part of the trail of the "Teragnole", Trentino women who crossed the Borcola pass from the Val Terragnolo down into the Val Posina.

trails.name: F14 - San Domenico - Alpe Coatè
trails.why: The route takes place on a path alternating with asphalt and tractors

trails.name: Similaun summit
trails.why: The Similaun is a mountain in the Schnalskamm group of the Ötztal Alps.

trails.name: Hinterer Seelenkogel - Cima delle Anime summit

points.name: Hinterer Seelenkogel - Cima delle Anime, 3,475 m

trails.why: The Hinterer Seelenkogel is a mountain in the Gurgler Kamm group of the Ötztal Alps.

trails.name: Sonklarspitze - Cima di Malavalle summit
trails.why: The Sonklarspitze, also Sonklarspitz, is a mountain in the Stubai Alps on the border between Tyrol, Austria, and South Tyrol, Italy.

trails.name: Hoher Weißzint - Punta Bianca summit
trails.why: The Hoher Weißzint is a mountain in the Zillertal Alps on the border between Tyrol, Austria, and South Tyrol, Italy.

trails.name: Östlicher Feuerstein - Montarso Orientale summit
trails.why: The Feuersteine are a twin summit on the main ridge of the Stubai Alps, right on the border between South Tyrol and Tyrol.

trails.name: III. Hornspitze (Berliner Spitze) summit
trails.why: The III. Hornspitze is a mountain in the Zillertal Alps on the border between Tyrol, Austria, and South Tyrol, Italy.

trails.name: Schneespitze - Monte della Neve
trails.why: The Monte della Neve is a mountain of the Stubai Alps on the Italian-Austrian border.

trails.name: Scheiberkogel - Cima Rocciosa summit
trails.why: The Cima Rocciosa is a mountain of the Passeier Alps on the Italian-Austrian border.

trails.name: Roter Grat - Cresta Rossa summit
trails.why: The Rote Grat is a 3,099 m mountain on the border of Tyrol and South Tyrol, now climbed glacier-free from the Nürnberger Hütte.

trails.name: Weißwandspitze - Parete Bianca summit
trails.why: The Weißwandspitze is a mountain in the Stubai Alps on the border between Tyrol, Austria, and South Tyrol, Italy.

trails.name: Bergkastelspitze - Cima Castello summit
trails.why: The Cima Castello is a mountain on the Italian-Austrian border, about six km south-east of Nauders.

trails.name: Klopaier Spitze summit
trails.why: The Klopaierspitze is a peak in the Ötztal Alps on the border between Tyrol, Austria, and South Tyrol, Italy.

trails.name: Piz Lad summit
trails.why: Piz Lad is a mountain of the Sesvenna Range, located on the border between Italy and Switzerland.

trails.name: Teplitzerhütte - Rifugio Vedretta Pendente hut
